correctness.rationale: The global C1 logarithmic-state conjugacy is exact. Every transformed trajectory differs from s-2 cos(t) by at most 2π epsilon(p+r), giving a global uniform return-displacement bound. Arcsine convolution and its distributional second-derivative identity establish an ODE for the profile. A strict elementary integral lower bound proves I(0)>2; a Wronskian monotonicity argument proves one positive maximum and hence the simple 2–4–0 profile-root count. Transverse-crossing C1 persistence yields exactly the same finite number for all sufficiently small positive epsilon and the stated Floquet signs. Infinite-range exclusion is analytic, not inferred from the checker. Critical levels and large epsilon remain unproved.

value.rationale: The first trigonometric harmonic is the restrictive natural Hilbert-number class investigated in the motivating work, whose known theorem gave only a large global upper bound. An exact open parameter region realizing four hyperbolic cycles, including complete neighboring two- and zero-cycle regions, provides a structurally meaningful lower-bound construction and stability data not supplied by arbitrary-harmonic existence. The response-profile shape is a nontrivial analytic lemma with a global root exclusion rather than a parameter renaming or a finite simulation.
